tasks.title: Admin panel: users, RBAC role assignments, on-call rotation/escalation, per-module enablement

scenarios: The admin panel manages users, roles, on-call, and modules

tasks.status_evidence: CORRECTION 2026-08-23 (an earlier annotation in this same batch claimed "the backend halves exist, so it is a console surface over existing APIs" — that was asserted, not checked, and it is WRONG). Verified against the tree: core/auth.Principal is {SourceID, Method, Admin} — a BINARY admin flag, not RBAC roles; there is no user directory and no user/role CRUD route in core/httpapi/router.go; operator_sessions is a session table, not a user store; escalation_queue is a dropped-escalation REQUEUE lane, not an on-call rotation; and a module's Enabled is OBSERVED from configuration, not writable. So T-010-8 needs BACKEND authority built first (a user/role model, an on-call rotation store, a module-enable write), and whether TG should own a user directory at all is a design question — approvers already come from LDAP/OIDC and policy approve_by. This is an owner-surface decision followed by several slices, not a console panel over existing APIs.
